project: The Stock Market: From the Ground Up
ownerDecision: B01 Owner-approved Beta Candidate; beta testers precede production-member acceptance; B02 work may proceed in parallel

scope.gradingMode: same private versioned engine; never publish raw answer keys

instructionalRules: Teach definitions and demonstrate before prediction or graded assessment
One fictional OHLCV decision pause at a time, no future bars or lookahead
Talia provides corrective explanation, scaffolded retry and independent transfer
Separate observation, inference, invalidation, no-trade and execution uncertainty
Preserve current private B02 v96 drafts; author new private versions only after individual review
No new Lab IDs, paid products, premium entitlements or live trading simulator claims
Keep any protected keyed answer, grader config and learner private data out of the public repository

labs.canonicalTitle: Premarket Information Release and Repricing
labs.learningObjective: Distinguish a source publication time from a later quote update and a later learner decision.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: A fictional filing timestamp at 08:04 ET, a verified public-access timestamp at 08:06, and a quote update at 08:09.
labs.guidedDecision: At an 08:08 pause, select only information proved available and delivered by then.
labs.independentTransfer: Repeat using a delayed distribution at 08:12 that invalidates a claim about the 08:08 decision.
labs.riskBoundary: Timestamp order alone does not prove that the filing caused the repricing or that the quote was tradable.

labs.canonicalTitle: Bid, Ask, Last, Spread, and Midpoint in a Frequently Updating Quote
labs.learningObjective: Define the bid, ask, last-trade price, displayed spread and mathematical midpoint without treating quotes as fills.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: At one fictional snapshot, best bid $10.00, best ask $10.08, most recent print $10.12; examine their separate timestamps.
labs.guidedDecision: Identify what a hypothetical buy or sell can and cannot infer from this snapshot.
labs.independentTransfer: Re-evaluate after a new best bid arrives without assuming the earlier last trade is current.
labs.riskBoundary: Top-of-book prices, midpoint and last prints do not establish available size, routing or execution.

labs.canonicalTitle: Compare Quote Width Without Jumping Ahead to Liquidity Analysis
labs.learningObjective: Compare absolute and percentage quoted spreads while holding time and price scale constant.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: Two fictional synchronized $10 quotes have displayed spreads of $0.03 and $0.12.
labs.guidedDecision: Describe which shown spread is wider and what further evidence is needed before ranking fill quality.
labs.independentTransfer: Compare new fictional quotes at different price scales; normalize widths before comparing.
labs.riskBoundary: A narrower quote alone cannot prove depth, persistence, a realistic round-trip cost or an actual fill.

labs.canonicalTitle: Raw 5-Minute Volume and Why the Timeframe Must Be Recorded
labs.learningObjective: Define traded-share volume for a completed bar and preserve the aggregation interval.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: A fictional completed five-minute bar records 80,000 shares; separately show five complete one-minute totals and verify their sum.
labs.guidedDecision: Describe the volume observation and state the full bar time range.
labs.independentTransfer: Compare a one-minute observation and a five-minute observation without claiming they are directly equivalent.
labs.riskBoundary: Volume counts completed transactions, not future directional momentum or the orders available now.

labs.canonicalTitle: Compare Lower Trading Activity With the Prior Exercise
labs.learningObjective: Compare volume for equal-duration completed bars and define the reference period.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: A completed five-minute bar records 12,000 shares after a completed 40,000-share bar.
labs.guidedDecision: Compute an observational ratio before describing the activity change.
labs.independentTransfer: Repeat with an unequal-duration bar and refuse a raw-volume-only comparison.
labs.riskBoundary: One pair of bars cannot establish normal volume, participant motivation, daily liquidity or executable size.

labs.canonicalTitle: High Volume Still Requires Liquidity and Order-Size Context
labs.learningObjective: Separate cumulative historical prints from live quoted depth and order-execution risk.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: A fictional 800,000-share completed bar coexists with a thin current ask and a much larger hypothetical incoming buy order.
labs.guidedDecision: Ask what the bar volume supports and whether a large order can be promised a fill at the displayed ask.
labs.independentTransfer: Repeat with unchanged historical volume but a different current spread and size.
labs.riskBoundary: High past volume is not guaranteed immediate liquidity, a tight spread or low slippage.

labs.canonicalTitle: Axes and Chart Types — Same Historical Window, Different Representation
labs.learningObjective: Identify axis units and separate closes-only line charts from OHLC candlesticks over identical completed periods.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: Show the same fictional three completed OHLC bars as both a line through closes and a candle view.
labs.guidedDecision: Identify facts lost when a line shows only closes while retaining the same timestamps.
labs.independentTransfer: Replot without changing price scale or interval and compare inferable high-low information.
labs.riskBoundary: A chart-style change must not invent historical bars, price events or forecasting power.

labs.canonicalTitle: Chart Type Versus Aggregation — Change One Variable at a Time
labs.learningObjective: Distinguish visual style from time-bucket aggregation and prevent incomplete-bar lookahead.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: Five completed fictional one-minute bars combine into one completed five-minute OHLC candle.
labs.guidedDecision: Change only chart type, then only interval, noting which values and timestamps genuinely change.
labs.independentTransfer: Explain why a currently forming five-minute bar cannot be treated as completed at an earlier pause.
labs.riskBoundary: Combining periods can conceal intrabar sequencing; aggregation does not authorize use of future observations.

labs.canonicalTitle: Construct an Up / Bullish Candle
labs.learningObjective: Calculate a bullish real body and both wicks using valid fictional OHLC ordering.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: Completed fictional OHLC: open $10.00, high $10.60, low $9.90, close $10.40.
labs.guidedDecision: Identify the upward real body, range and upper/lower wick without assuming order of intrabar prints.
labs.independentTransfer: Swap the opening and closing prices while preserving a physically valid high and low.
labs.riskBoundary: A bullish candle does not prove buyer identity, future gains or whether the close was fillable.

labs.canonicalTitle: Construct a Down / Bearish Candle
labs.learningObjective: Calculate a bearish real body, high-low range and wick lengths without treating a red body as a forecast.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: Completed fictional OHLC: open $10.50, high $10.60, low $10.00, close $10.20.
labs.guidedDecision: Identify the down body and both wick distances using completed data only.
labs.independentTransfer: Create another valid down candle with a smaller real body but unchanged total range.
labs.riskBoundary: Color alone cannot establish trading intent, next-bar direction or the chronological order of extremes.

labs.canonicalTitle: Identify an Exact or Near Doji
labs.learningObjective: Differentiate exact open-equals-close equality from a context-dependent near-doji judgment.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: One fictional candle opens and closes at $10.00; another closes one cent above a $10.00 open.
labs.guidedDecision: Classify the exact doji mathematically and identify the information needed to judge near-doji significance.
labs.independentTransfer: Compare one-cent bodies against different bar ranges and price scales.
labs.riskBoundary: Near-doji has no universal one-cent rule; a small body does not establish an impending reversal.

labs.canonicalTitle: Large Up Body, Close Near High
labs.learningObjective: Compare real-body size with total range and close position using completed OHLC evidence.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: Fictional completed candle opens $10.00, closes $10.60, has high $10.65 and low $9.85.
labs.guidedDecision: Describe body-to-range proportion and the close's distance below the high.
labs.independentTransfer: Re-evaluate a new candle with the same close but a much higher high.
labs.riskBoundary: A high-position close describes this bar; it is not a guarantee of breakout follow-through.

labs.canonicalTitle: Large Down Body, Close Near Low
labs.learningObjective: Compare a bearish body against its high-low range and measure the close's proximity to the low.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: Fictional completed candle opens $11.00, closes $10.30, has high $11.10 and low $10.25.
labs.guidedDecision: Measure the real body, full range and distance of the close above the low.
labs.independentTransfer: Compare a similar down close after a smaller completed intrabar range.
labs.riskBoundary: The appearance does not prove aggressive sellers, a tradable short entry or lower future prices.

labs.canonicalTitle: Long Lower Wick, Recovery Into the Close
labs.learningObjective: Calculate lower-wick size and discuss recovery as observed price behavior, not verified support.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: Fictional completed candle opens $10.40, dips to $9.70, reaches $10.50 and closes $10.35.
labs.guidedDecision: Separate the lower excursion from the final close and identify the low-to-close recovery.
labs.independentTransfer: Contrast with a later completed candle that breaks below the prior low.
labs.riskBoundary: A lower wick cannot prove that support will hold, identify resting bids or reveal the sequence of all trades.

labs.canonicalTitle: Long Upper Wick, Close Back Near the Lower Area
labs.learningObjective: Describe an upper-wick excursion and return toward the lower part of a completed candle.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: Fictional completed candle opens $10.00, peaks $10.70, bottoms $9.95 and closes $10.10.
labs.guidedDecision: Calculate upper-wick distance and describe what the final close actually establishes.
labs.independentTransfer: Compare to another bar that subsequently closes above the earlier peak.
labs.riskBoundary: An upper wick alone is not a reliable reversal signal or evidence of identified institutional selling.

labs.canonicalTitle: Small Body With Two-Sided Excursion
labs.learningObjective: Distinguish a small real body from a wide intrabar range with nonzero upper and lower wicks.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: Fictional completed candle opens $10.00, has high $10.40 and low $9.60, and closes $10.03.
labs.guidedDecision: Compare the body with the full range and identify both wicks.
labs.independentTransfer: Re-evaluate the same small body with a narrow range; describe why visual interpretation changes.
labs.riskBoundary: Two-sided wicks are not proof that buyer and seller power was exactly equal or that reversal is inevitable.

labs.canonicalTitle: Exact Doji With Unequal Wicks
labs.learningObjective: Explain that exact open-equals-close does not imply equal upper and lower excursions.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: Fictional completed OHLC: open and close $10.00, high $10.15, low $9.50.
labs.guidedDecision: Confirm body size and compute asymmetric wicks without inferring intrabar trade order.
labs.independentTransfer: Contrast with an exact doji with symmetric wicks and the same ending price.
labs.riskBoundary: Equal open and close is a mathematical relation, not proof of neutral flow or an objective trend signal.

labs.canonicalTitle: Upward Follow-Through With Contracting Ranges
labs.learningObjective: Recognize sequential higher completed closes and contracting high-low ranges on a fixed timeframe.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: Three fictional completed five-minute candles close progressively higher while each completed high-low range narrows.
labs.guidedDecision: Identify what the sequence demonstrates, and distinguish it from accelerating momentum.
labs.independentTransfer: Add a fourth completed bar with a lower close and reassess the sequence without retroactively changing prior reads.
labs.riskBoundary: Contracting range amid higher closes does not prove breakout continuation, depth or reliable future direction.

labs.canonicalTitle: Downward Follow-Through
labs.learningObjective: Identify genuine completed downward follow-through using comparable bars and consistent clocks.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: Three fictional completed five-minute bars show lower closes; examine whether lows and ranges corroborate the description.
labs.guidedDecision: State precisely which candle-to-candle comparisons are observed and which are still unproven.
labs.independentTransfer: Include a fourth bar with a higher close; update the observation rather than asserting an inevitable trend.
labs.riskBoundary: A few lower closes do not alone justify a short trade, a fill assumption or an unrestricted stop.

labs.canonicalTitle: Directional Follow-Through Interrupted by an Opposite Expansion
labs.learningObjective: Identify an opposite-direction expanded-range bar that interrupts, but need not permanently reverse, prior follow-through.
labs.fictionalDemonstration: Two completed fictional upward candles are followed by a completed down candle with a wider high-low range.
labs.guidedDecision: Describe the interruption and the evidence required before labeling an actual structure reversal.
labs.independentTransfer: Use a subsequent completed bar that resumes upward closes and revise the narrative.
labs.riskBoundary: One counterdirectional expansion does not establish a permanent trend reversal, executable trade or hindsight-independent prediction.
